added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(A_{n,m,\tau}:=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\) and \(L_m:=\log(2m)\). There are constants \(0<c_{\beta,D}\leq C_{\beta,D}<\infty\), depending only on \(\beta,D\), with the following properties for every admissible \(n,m,\tau\). If
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}\geq L_m^{1-\varkappa},                                       \tag{42}
\]
then
\[
c_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)
\leq \mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\leq C_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau).                       \tag{43}
\]
The upper inequality is attained by the computable total learner \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{tail}}\), and the lower inequality holds over the same \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\) against every learner in \(\mathfrak A_{n,m}\). Thus (42) is the familywise-testing phase in which the coordinatewise rate is unavoidable, including when the risk saturates at order \(\ell\).

If instead \(A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa}\), then the established bounds localize to
\[
c_{\beta,D}\min\!\left\{\ell,
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\right]\right\}
\leq \mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\leq C_{\beta,D}\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}.               \tag{44}
\]
Consequently, along admissible sequences with \(n\to\infty\), the condition \(A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\to0\) is sufficient for \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\), whereas \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\) implies \(A_{n,m,\tau}\to0\) and hence eventual membership in the strict sub-familywise phase. No sequence visiting (42) infinitely often has vanishing regret. Moreover, every sequence on which \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\) satisfies
\[
\frac{\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)}{\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}(n,m)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{45}
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write
\[
q_N:=\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\},\quad
A:=\ell q_N,\quad L:=\log(2m).
\]
These are proof-local abbreviations. By the definition \(N=n/m\),
\[
\left\{\frac{m\log(2m)}n\right\}^{\varkappa}
=\left(\frac LN\right)^{\varkappa}.                                    \tag{46}
\]
Since \(m\geq2\), \(L\geq\log4>1\). We claim that the definition in \(\mathrm{def{:}coordinatewise\text{-}hall\text{-}baseline}\) obeys the exact identity
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)=\min\{\ell,AL^{\varkappa}\}.          \tag{47}
\]
Indeed, if \(N\geq1\), then \(q_N=N^{-\varkappa}\), and (46) gives (47). If \(N<1\), then \(q_N=1\), \(L/N>1\), and \(L^{\varkappa}>1\). Hence both
\(\ell\min\{1,(L/N)^{\varkappa}\}\) and \(\min\{\ell,AL^{\varkappa}\}\) equal \(\ell\). This proves (47) in all cases.

The definition \(\varkappa=\beta/(2\beta+4)\), together with \(\beta>0\), gives \(0<\varkappa<1\), so \(\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)>0\). Suppose first that \(A\geq L^{1-\varkappa}\). Raising this inequality to the positive power \(\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)\) gives
\[
A^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\geq
\left(L^{1-\varkappa}\right)^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}=L^{\varkappa}.   \tag{48}
\]
Thus the inner minimum in \(\mathrm{prop{:}multiscale\text{-}paired\text{-}splice\text{-}lower\text{-}envelope}\) is exactly \(L^{\varkappa}\). That proposition and monotonicity of \(u\mapsto\min\{\ell,u\}\) imply
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
&\geq c_{\beta,D}\min\{\ell,A(1+L^{\varkappa})\}\\
&\geq c_{\beta,D}\min\{\ell,AL^{\varkappa}\}
=c_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau),                       \tag{49}
\end{split}
\]
where the last equality is (47). The upper half of \(\mathrm{thm{:}generic\text{-}regret\text{-}sandwich}\), again using (47), gives
\[
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\leq C_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau).                    \tag{50}
\]
The same theorem identifies \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{tail}}\) as the measurable data-driven witness for (50), while \(\mathrm{prop{:}multiscale\text{-}paired\text{-}splice\text{-}lower\text{-}envelope}\) states that (49) uses laws in the same Hall class and ranges against every measurable randomized learner. This proves (43), including the case in which either minimum in (49)--(50) equals \(\ell\).

The familywise phase cannot have vanishing regret. In fact, (42) gives
\[
AL^{\varkappa}\geq L^{1-\varkappa}L^{\varkappa}=L.                     \tag{51}
\]
The restrictions \(m\geq2\), \(n\geq2\), and \(\tau\leq1/(8n)\) give respectively \(L\geq\log4\) and \(\ell=\log(1/\tau)\geq\log(8n)\geq\log16\). Equations (47), (49), and (51) therefore yield
\[
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\geq c_{\beta,D}\log4                              \tag{52}
\]
whenever (42) holds. Thus a sequence satisfying (42) infinitely often cannot have regret tending to zero.

Now suppose \(A<L^{1-\varkappa}\). The same positive-power calculation as in (48), with a strict inequality, gives
\[
A^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}<L^{\varkappa}.                              \tag{53}
\]
Substitution of (53) into \(\mathrm{prop{:}multiscale\text{-}paired\text{-}splice\text{-}lower\text{-}envelope}\) proves the lower inequality in (44); equations (47) and (50) prove its upper inequality. In particular, if \(AL^{\varkappa}\to0\), (44) implies \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\).

Conversely, the multiscale lower envelope is at least
\[
c_{\beta,D}\min\{\ell,A\},                                            \tag{54}
\]
because its bracketed factor is at least one. Along every admissible sequence with \(n\to\infty\), the tail restriction gives \(\ell\geq\log(8n)\to\infty\). If \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\to0\), (54) consequently forces \(A\to0\). Since \(L^{1-\varkappa}\geq(\log4)^{1-\varkappa}>1\), this also forces the strict inequality (53) eventually.

Finally, \(A=\ell q_N\to0\) and \(\ell\to\infty\) imply \(q_N\to0\). By the definition of \(q_N\), this entails \(N\to\infty\), and hence eventually
\[
\frac mn=N^{-1}\longrightarrow0,\quad
\ell\left(\frac mn\right)^{\varkappa}=\ell N^{-\varkappa}=A\longrightarrow0. \tag{55}
\]
The final assertion of \(\mathrm{thm{:}generic\text{-}regret\text{-}sandwich}\), applied using (55), is exactly (45). This completes the proof.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem closes the entire familywise-testing phase, identifies the exact elbow including saturation, and confines the remaining many-cell regret problem to the strict sub-familywise phase.
added_lemmas.gap: CarpentierKim2015 motivates the translated coordinatewise one-tail benchmark but does not prove its minimax necessity for a randomized capacity-selected mixture; the paired-splice lower envelope supplies that missing converse exactly at and above the elbow.
added_lemmas.consumer: For the non-nested upper-cost-quantile objective of OsamaZachariahStoica2020, the theorem certifies that familywise tail learning is unavoidable in this Hall model and that policy learning is not statistically justified there in a vanishing-regret sense.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question still asks for the familywise phase, but the accepted multiscale lower envelope and the existing coordinatewise upper theorem now match exactly whenever \(A_{n,m,\tau}\geq L_m^{1-\varkappa}\). The only honest unresolved scope is the strict complementary phase.

proposed.name: paired-splice soft-loss frontier handle
proposed.construction: Tensorize two-arm Hall splices across paired cells at an arbitrary admissible amplitude, retain the exact logarithmic mixture loss, condition on the pair sample counts, factor the product posterior, and compare every feasible zero/one/two-cell capacity allocation with one posterior-MAP action per pair by concavity. A binomial lower-tail calculation followed by amplitude optimization gives the multiscale same-class lower envelope. Comparing that envelope with the separate coordinatewise sorting-and-inversion upper witness closes the familywise phase \(\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\geq[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\), including saturation. Below this elbow the construction supplies the lower expression with \([\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}]^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\), but no localized selected-mixture upper witness; equality of the two bounds is not part of the construction there.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The handle predates the proved comparison. Its post-image must distinguish the now-closed familywise phase from the still-open localized selected-mixture upper problem below the exact elbow.

The dependency spine now records the proved familywise theorem and leaves the open node responsible only for the strict sub-familywise phase; its proposed claim is supplied through the paired statement narrowing.

proposed.comparator_claim: Equation (4) supplies a marginal upper-cost-quantile decision objective and its conformal limit can become uninformative when support information is inadequate; it is a non-nested consumer anchor, not a Hall-class inclusion or a rate engine.

Theorem 1 bounds constrained-policy regret for regular mean welfare by a policy-complexity and efficient-score scale; every vanishing-regret sequence in the present extreme-tail model has regret asymptotically larger than the corresponding regular cell-policy scale.
The paper estimates a policy maximizing a fixed marginal potential-outcome quantile and derives nonstandard fixed-level asymptotics.

Its one-tail Hall results motivate the coordinatewise benchmark after the translation \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\). Each conditional tail here is a compact translated slice of that one-tail class, while the full randomized \(2m\)-tail causal experiment is a stricter product construction. The translated coordinatewise benchmark is minimax-equivalent in the familywise phase, but the strict sub-familywise capacity-mixture upper frontier does not follow from their theorems.
The paper develops extreme-value inference for the average distribution of predetermined heterogeneous power-law observations.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds honest scalar tail confidence length by worst-case bias and the paper constructs a bias-aware interval.
Theorems 4.3 and 5.1 give process inference for extreme treatment contrasts over tail levels and fixed treatment pairs.
The manuscript derives finite-sample minimax-regret treatment rules for a fixed quantile with outcomes restricted to the unit interval.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Comparator positioning must record the new phasewise equivalence to the translated Carpentier--Kim benchmark and the proved all-vanishing-regime separation from the regular-policy scale, while retaining Osama--Zachariah--Stoica as a non-nested consumer anchor.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Within \(A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa}\), match the proved lower expression with one computable learner over the full heterogeneous Hall class, or exhibit a harder same-class configuration; thereby decide the exact vanishing criterion and the maximal strict-improvement regimes relative to \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Simultaneous coordinatewise control attains only \(\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}\). The missing oracle inequality must instead control the random mixture mass of severely underestimated arms selected under capacity, uniformly over heterogeneous indices and local ties; the frozen primitives provide no such localized selected-mixture concentration result.
open_obligations.attempted: The paired product-prior converse, fixed-sample posterior factorization, capacity exchange, binomial missed-cell lower bound, and amplitude optimization already close the lower side. A natural-threshold empirical minimizer and an average multiplicative core comparison were also tried, but rare severe underestimation can be selected adaptively; restoring simultaneous control reproduces the coordinatewise logarithmic factor.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Put \(A_{n,m,\tau}:=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\) and \(L_m:=\log(2m)\). The familywise phase is now closed:
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}\geq L_m^{1-\varkappa}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\asymp_{\beta,D}
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)
=\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}.
\]
This comparison includes saturation, and the risk is bounded away from zero throughout that phase. In the complementary phase the proved bracket is
\[
c_{\beta,D}\min\!\left\{\ell,
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\right]\right\}
\leq\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\leq C_{\beta,D}\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}.
\]
Hence \(A_{n,m,\tau}\to0\) is necessary for vanishing regret, while \(A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\to0\) is sufficient. Every vanishing-regret sequence satisfies \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)/\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}(n,m)\to\infty\). The remaining issue is only the sub-familywise selected-mixture upper bound, or a harder same-class lower configuration.

prose_updates.tldr: Capacity-constrained treatment choice at a beyond-sample loss quantile is governed by the inverse of a selected heterogeneous survival mixture. The coordinatewise upper bound is now proved minimax-sharp throughout the familywise phase \(A_{n,m,\tau}\geq[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\), including saturation, and regret cannot vanish there. Below that exact elbow, the multiscale same-class lower envelope and coordinatewise upper bound leave a localized selected-mixture gap. The simultaneous-inference width converse and exact shrinking criterion remain a separate open question.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-level quantile-policy methods do not address extrapolated Hall tails. One-tail Hall theory supplies the translated coordinatewise benchmark, which is now proved unavoidable in the familywise phase, but neither it nor regular policy-learning theory supplies the capacity-aware oracle inequality needed below the exact elbow.
project_justification.niche: For each fixed even cell count, randomization identifies every policy mixture and capacity optimization is computable by sorting. Heterogeneous indices, local ties, empty observed cells, and growing mixture mass remain in the model; the paired-splice argument handles unrestricted reallocation and isolates the strict sub-familywise phase where selected-mixture averaging could improve on familywise estimation.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the generic full-class regret sandwich, the exact two-cell frontier, a multiscale paired-splice lower envelope, and the matched coordinatewise frontier whenever \(A_{n,m,\tau}\geq[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\). It proves that every vanishing-regret sequence is sub-familywise and remains asymptotically separated from the regular additive-policy benchmark. The only remaining regret problem is the exact upper frontier below the elbow; confidence-width optimality remains separate.

prose_updates.related_work: CarpentierKim2015 is one-tail statistical substrate, not a capacity-policy theorem. Each conditional tail in this note is a compact translated slice of its one-tail Hall class after the parameter conversion \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\), while the full randomized causal experiment couples \(2m\) such tails through a stricter product construction. The present paired-splice converse and coordinatewise upper bound together prove equivalence to the translated coordinatewise benchmark only in the familywise phase; below the elbow, CarpentierKim2015 supplies no selected-mixture oracle inequality. A paired-splice converse transfers upward only to an explicitly defined superclass containing every constructed full-data law; an upper bound must be rechecked on that superclass and does not transfer from the splice. AtheyWager2021 and KitagawaTetenov2018 concern regular additive welfare, and the proved implication \(\mathcal R/\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}\to\infty\) on every vanishing-regret sequence shows that their \(\sqrt{m/n}\)-type scale is not the extreme-tail frontier. WangZhouSongSherwood2018 and XiaZhangKong2026 occupy fixed-level quantile-policy identification or learning. OsamaZachariahStoica2020 supplies the non-nested marginal upper-cost-quantile consumer objective; it is neither a class-inclusion statement nor a rate engine for this Hall experiment. Its support-based conformal limit motivates the extrapolation question but does not establish the answer. Predetermined heterogeneous-tail pooling, scalar tail intervals, and fixed-pair extreme-treatment inference likewise do not resolve selection among capacity-constrained mixtures.
prose_updates.interpretation: The elbow compares extrapolation difficulty \(A_{n,m,\tau}=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\) with the amount of familywise testing information \([\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\). At and above the elbow, rare cellwise errors accumulate enough exact logarithmic mixture loss that coordinatewise calibration is minimax-unavoidable and regret stays nonzero. Below it, the lower experiment charges only the smaller selected-mixture term; whether a learner can realize that averaging gain uniformly is the remaining question.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The distributional lower-side obstruction is resolved, and comparison with the existing coordinatewise upper theorem closes the familywise phase exactly, including saturation. The residual regret step is confined to \(A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa}\): no proved learner controls data-dependent selected tail weights at the lower rate without reverting to the coordinatewise maximum. Thus \(A_{n,m,\tau}\to0\) is proved necessary and \(A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\to0\) sufficient for vanishing regret, but equality of these criteria remains open. The confidence-width converse and exact shrinking condition remain separately open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established claims are the fixed-cell Hall model and identification setup, sorting and inversion, Hall-core approximation, the local-dominance map, the generic coordinatewise regret sandwich, the exact two-cell rate, the simultaneous confidence upper system, the multiscale paired-splice lower envelope, and the matched familywise regret frontier at \(A_{n,m,\tau}\geq[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\). The lower envelope is not described as the exact frontier below that elbow. The exact sub-familywise capacity-aware upper rate and the sharp confidence-width frontier remain open. No common tail index, fixed gap, density, nonempty realized cell sample, nuisance-rate assumption, or selection penalty is imposed. A paired-splice converse may be exported only to a superclass explicitly containing its full-data laws; the corresponding upper bound requires a separate proof.

statement_notes.justification: The familywise phase and the all-vanishing-regime regular-policy comparison are now settled; the remaining headline contribution is exactly the localized selected-mixture frontier below the elbow.
statement_notes.gap: CarpentierKim2015 supplies translated one-tail familywise machinery but no randomized capacity-selected mixture oracle inequality below the elbow, and AtheyWager2021 supplies no moving extreme-mixture rate.
statement_notes.consumer: Resolving the sub-familywise gap would tell users of the non-nested upper-cost-quantile objective in OsamaZachariahStoica2020 exactly when capacity averaging permits reliable Hall extrapolation beyond the now-certified familywise obstruction.
